text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 1.97% today, extending a sharp two-week decline of 7.67%. The main driver appears to be a significant shift in market sentiment around refinery stocks—CNBC reported directly on November 23rd that "the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding," signaling that investors are rotating out of the energy refining trade that has been a major profit engine. This comes as oil prices have held relatively stable (US crude at $89.53/barrel) and refineries run near full capacity at 95.7%, so the move is fundamentally about investor appetite changing rather than refining economics breaking down.

The broader context reinforces this pivot. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—including Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries and Iranian threats—had previously supported energy prices and refinery margins, but that bullish narrative may be fading in the market's eyes. Combined with the climate summit developments and broader economic uncertainty, money that flooded into refinery stocks during their boom cycle appears to be flowing elsewhere.
